decision: KEEP_V24  (do NOT proceed to new architecture / Candidate A or B on current evidence)
single_seed_v24_caveat: v24 scored at seed42 only; no CI on v24 itself. All ablations are 3-seed. A formal §7 promotion CI requires >=3 v24 seeds (not run). Decision made on point estimates + ablation SDs.

simple_ESM_matches_v24.answer: NO in oracle frame (v24 0.530 > best simple B3 0.455); BUT v24 not deployably robust

MoE_reproducible_benefit.answer: NO (non-monotonic: B7 removes MoE+contacts+v18=0.485 > B5 removes only MoE=0.438). Co-dependent stack, not clean component justification

contacts_help_seqonly.answer: Ambiguous: B6(-contacts) 0.477 < v24 0.530, but single-seed v24 + co-dependence; and content edge over prior is p53/POU-driven & n.s.

Nchain_helps_multimers.answer: Not cleanly testable: no 'v24 without N-chain' ablation (B5/B6/B7 all keep N-chain). Recorded as a design gap.

any_variant_beats_family_prior_deployabl.answer: NO. Every trained variant (incl. ablations) <= family prior (B0 0.518-0.539) on end-to-end covR; only single-seed v24 reaches it.

advantage_robust_to_registration.answer: NO. Under canonical (no-peeking) registration everything collapses ~4-10x and B1(nearest) > v24 (0.070 vs 0.045 pred-only). v24's lead is oracle-registration-dependent.

recommendation: Keep v24 as the current model. Do NOT start Set-Transformer / interface-mixer / v25 work: the necessity audit shows no component provides a robust, reproducible, deployable gain, and no variant beats a family-average prior under an honest (canonical) registration. If revisited: (1) train >=3 v24 seeds, (2) adopt a canonical/deployable primary metric (oracle registration masks the real gap), (3) fix the benchmark's registration difficulty before claiming architecture gains.
